questions.stem: « En France, beaucoup de familles prennent encore le temps de déjeuner ensemble le dimanche, un repas qui peut durer tout l'après-midi. » What does this suggest about French lifestyles?
options: Most families now skip lunch on Sundays
Sunday lunch is a quick meal before going out
Families usually eat at restaurants on Sundays
Shared meals remain an important social ritual
questions.explanation: A meal that « peut durer tout l'après-midi » and that families « prennent encore le temps » to share shows how much the ritual is valued. Nothing suggests a quick meal or eating out.

questions.stem: What is « le goûter »?
options: a mid-morning coffee break for office workers
a drink with nibbles before dinner
a light supper late in the evening
an afternoon snack, especially for children
questions.explanation: « Le goûter » is the snack children eat after school, around 4.30 pm. Drinks and nibbles before dinner are « l'apéritif », or « l'apéro » in everyday speech.

questions.stem: « On se retrouve pour l'apéro vers 19 heures ? » What is being proposed?
options: a late lunch together at a café
a coffee together before work
dessert together after the evening meal
drinks and nibbles before dinner
questions.explanation: « L'apéro » (short for « l'apéritif ») is a drink with snacks before the evening meal, a relaxed social habit. The time, 7 pm, fits the hour before a French dinner.

questions.stem: In 2010 UNESCO listed « le repas gastronomique des Français » as intangible cultural heritage. What does the listing recognise?
options: the custom of a festive meal shared over several courses
the recipes served in famous Paris restaurants
the professional skills of France's leading chefs
the quality of the wines and cheeses made in French regions
questions.explanation: UNESCO recognised a social practice: marking important moments with a carefully chosen meal of several courses, eaten together and talked about at the table. It is the shared custom, not chefs or restaurant recipes, that is listed.

questions.stem: « Grâce à leurs RTT, beaucoup de salariés partent en week-end prolongé. » What are « les RTT »?
options: days off that make up for hours worked beyond the 35-hour week
public holidays that happen to fall on a Monday or Friday
unpaid leave that employees take between two jobs
the paid summer holidays that most workers take in August
questions.explanation: RTT stands for « réduction du temps de travail ». Employees who work more than the legal 35-hour week earn extra days off in return. Public holidays are « les jours fériés ».

questions.stem: What does « faire le pont » mean?
options: to stay late at work to finish an urgent project
to take off the working day between a holiday and a weekend
to commute across the city to get to work each day
to cross a border to do cheaper shopping in another country
questions.explanation: If a public holiday falls on a Thursday, many people « font le pont » by taking Friday off too, giving a four-day weekend. The 'bridge' links the holiday to the weekend.

questions.stem: « Le dimanche, la plupart des commerces sont fermés, sauf la boulangerie le matin. » What does this tell a visitor?
options: Shops open only on Sunday mornings, then close for the week
The bakery is the only shop in town that stays closed all day on Sunday
All shops stay open late on Sundays except the bakery
Most shops close on Sundays, but the bakery opens in the morning
questions.explanation: « Sauf » means 'except', so the bakery is the exception to the Sunday closing. The sentence says nothing about late opening.

questions.stem: What does « les heures de pointe » mean?
options: overtime hours
rush hour
opening hours
off-peak times
questions.explanation: « Les heures de pointe » are the busiest times on roads and public transport. Off-peak times are « les heures creuses ».

questions.stem: « En banlieue, il faut souvent une heure de RER pour aller travailler à Paris. » What is « la banlieue »?
options: the suburbs around a city
the historic city centre
the countryside far from towns
the business district of a city
questions.explanation: « La banlieue » is the ring of suburbs around a large city. The RER is the rail network that links the Paris suburbs with the centre.

questions.stem: What does « l'exode rural » describe?
options: farmers emigrating to work in other countries
the yearly rush of city holidaymakers to the coast in August
people leaving the countryside to live in cities
city dwellers moving out to live in the country
questions.explanation: An « exode » is a mass departure, and « rural » means from the countryside. The movement the other way, from city to country, is sometimes called « l'exode urbain ».

questions.stem: « Les néo-ruraux quittent les grandes villes pour s'installer à la campagne, attirés par un cadre de vie plus calme et des logements moins chers. » Who are « les néo-ruraux »?
options: young people born and raised in rural villages
tourists who rent country houses each summer
city dwellers who have moved to the countryside
farmers who have left the land to live in cities
questions.explanation: « Néo- » means new: they are new country residents who come from the cities, drawn by a calmer « cadre de vie » (living environment) and cheaper housing. People born in villages are not new arrivals.

questions.stem: « Ici, tout le monde se connaît, les commerces ferment à midi et il n'y a qu'un bus par jour. C'est paisible, mais pour les jeunes, c'est mort. » What is the speaker's view of village life?
options: lively, with plenty for teenagers to do
expensive and crowded with summer tourists
noisy because of the traffic through town
peaceful, but with nothing for young people
questions.explanation: « C'est paisible » is the positive, and « c'est mort » is slang for 'there's nothing going on'. One bus a day and shops closing at noon support that view.

questions.stem: Since 2002, what has « Paris Plages » offered Parisians each summer?
options: sand, deckchairs and activities along the Seine
cheap train fares to the Normandy beaches
free entry to the city's indoor swimming pools
a beach volleyball tournament at the Eiffel Tower
questions.explanation: Paris Plages turns stretches of the Seine's banks into a temporary beach, aimed at people who cannot go away on holiday. It is a free city event, not a transport deal.

questions.stem: Which label tells you a film is shown in its original language with French subtitles?
options: la version originale sous-titrée
la version française doublée
la version longue du film
la version restaurée du film
questions.explanation: Cinema listings shorten it to VOST: the original soundtrack with subtitles. « La version française » (VF) is dubbed into French, and « la version longue » is an extended cut.

questions.stem: What is « une avant-première »?
options: a short film shown before the main feature
a screening held before a film's general release
the opening scene that comes before the credits
the first week of a film's run in cinemas
questions.explanation: An « avant-première » is a preview screening, often with the director and actors present, before the film « sort en salle ». A short film is « un court métrage ».

questions.stem: What is « un long métrage »?
options: a short film
a documentary series
a trailer for a new film
a feature-length film
questions.explanation: « Un long métrage » is a feature film and « un court métrage » a short. A trailer is « une bande-annonce ».

questions.stem: « La bande originale du film est signée par un compositeur québécois. » What is « la bande originale »?
options: the opening credits
the soundtrack
the original script
the first edit of the film
questions.explanation: « La bande originale », often shortened to « la BO », is the film's music. The script is « le scénario » and the credits « le générique ».

questions.stem: In French, what is « le neuvième art »?
options: architecture
music
comics
cinema
questions.explanation: French numbers the arts, and comics, « la bande dessinée », are the ninth. Cinema is « le septième art ».

questions.stem: « Le film a fait un carton au box-office, mais la critique l'a descendu en flammes. » What happened?
options: Critics loved it, but few people went to see it
It was a hit with audiences and critics alike
It was withdrawn after a fire at the premiere
It was a commercial hit, but critics savaged it
questions.explanation: « Faire un carton » is informal for a big success, and « descendre en flammes » means to tear apart in criticism. The flames are figurative, not a real fire.

questions.stem: Review: « Malgré quelques longueurs, ce premier film tient ses promesses : on rit, on pleure, on en ressort ému. » What is the reviewer's verdict?
options: positive, despite a few slow passages
negative, because the film is far too long
mixed, praising the plot but not the acting
negative, as it fails to move the audience
questions.explanation: « Quelques longueurs » are some slow or overlong passages, conceded with « malgré ». The rest is praise: the film « tient ses promesses » and leaves viewers moved.

questions.stem: In music, what is « un tube »?
options: a hit song
a music video
a song lyric
a concert tour
questions.explanation: « Un tube » is informal for a hit. A music video is « un clip » and a tour « une tournée ».

questions.stem: « Les paroles de cette chanson évoquent l'exil et le mal du pays. » What are « les paroles » here?
options: the lyrics
the melody
the singer's interviews
the album cover
questions.explanation: « Les paroles » of a song are its words. The tune is « la mélodie » or « l'air ».

questions.stem: What is « une chanson à texte »?
options: a song spoken rather than sung over music
a song written to advertise a product
a song performed with no instruments
a song valued above all for its lyrics
questions.explanation: « La chanson à texte » is a French tradition in which the poetry of the words matters as much as the music. A song written for advertising is « un jingle ».

questions.stem: Since 1996, French music radio stations have had to play a minimum share of what kind of songs?
options: songs by European artists
live concert recordings
classical and jazz pieces
songs sung in French
questions.explanation: French law sets a quota of French-language songs on music radio, to protect the language and support French-speaking artists. It concerns the language of the songs, not where the artists come from.

questions.stem: Every January, the town of Angoulême hosts a major international festival of what?
options: jazz
comics
short films
street theatre
questions.explanation: The Festival international de la bande dessinée d'Angoulême, held since 1974, is one of the world's main comics festivals.

questions.stem: The Festival d'Avignon, founded in 1947 and held each July, is mainly a festival of what?
options: photography and painting
theatre and the performing arts
cinema and television drama
classical music and opera
questions.explanation: Founded by Jean Vilar, the Avignon festival is a major theatre festival, with an official programme and a huge fringe, « le Off ». The great film festival is at Cannes.

questions.stem: Every summer, Montréal hosts one of the world's largest festivals of which kind of music?
options: opera
country
folk dance
jazz
questions.explanation: The Festival international de jazz de Montréal fills the city centre with free outdoor concerts as well as ticketed ones.

questions.stem: What is « le surtourisme »?
options: tourism that takes place outside the busy season
travelling in a group with an official guide
travelling abroad on a very small budget
so many tourists that a place and its residents suffer
questions.explanation: « Sur- » means over: overtourism, as in crowded Venice or Mont-Saint-Michel. Tourism outside the busy season is « hors saison ».

questions.stem: What is « le tourisme durable »?
options: travel that is booked a long time in advance
long stays abroad taken by retired people
tours of historic monuments and castles
travel that limits harm to nature and local people
questions.explanation: « Durable » means sustainable here, not long-lasting. Sustainable tourism respects the environment and benefits the communities visited.

questions.stem: « Pendant mon échange au Sénégal, j'ai vécu un vrai choc culturel les premières semaines. » What did the writer experience?
options: a sudden passion for the local Senegalese music
disorientation on meeting an unfamiliar culture
an illness caught soon after arriving
an argument with the host family
questions.explanation: « Un choc culturel » is culture shock, the unsettled feeling of adjusting to different customs. It is common in the first weeks abroad.

questions.stem: What does « avoir le mal du pays » mean?
options: to dislike your own country
to miss your flight home
to be homesick
to be travel sick
questions.explanation: « Le mal du pays » is homesickness. Travel sickness is « le mal des transports ».

questions.stem: Which kind of accommodation is a room in someone's home, with breakfast included?
options: une chambre d'hôte
une auberge de jeunesse
un camping
un gîte
questions.explanation: « Une chambre d'hôte » is a bed and breakfast in the owner's house. « Un gîte » is a self-catering holiday house rented on its own.

questions.stem: « Partir seule à l'autre bout du monde m'a appris à me débrouiller : je ne parlais pas la langue, mais je me suis toujours fait comprendre. » What did the trip teach the writer?
options: never to travel again without a guide
to plan every day of a trip in detail
to cope alone and make herself understood
to speak the local language fluently
questions.explanation: « Se débrouiller » means to manage or cope, and « se faire comprendre » to make yourself understood. She says she did not speak the language, so fluency is ruled out.

questions.stem: « Voyager, ce n'est pas cocher des destinations sur une liste ; c'est accepter d'être dérouté. » What view does the writer express?
options: It is better to see few places in comfort
Real travel means being open to the unexpected
Travellers should keep a list of places to visit
Travel is only worthwhile with a good guide
questions.explanation: The « ce n'est pas… c'est… » structure rejects ticking off a list in favour of being « dérouté », thrown off course. The writer values surprise over planning.

questions.stem: Travel blog: « On a fait le tour de l'île en deux jours, mais on aurait pu y rester un mois ! » What does the writer mean?
options: They needed a whole month to get around the island
They were bored with the island after only two days
They could not leave the island because of bad weather
They saw it quickly but could happily have stayed far longer
questions.explanation: « On aurait pu » is the conditional perfect, 'we could have': the month is what they would have liked, not what happened. The tour itself took two days.

questions.stem: « Je pensais que les Québécois parlaient comme les Français. En fait, entre l'accent et les expressions, j'ai dû tendre l'oreille ! » What does the traveller report?
options: Québécois people refused to speak French to her
She understood Québec French easily from day one
She had to speak English the whole time in Québec
Québec French took real effort to follow at first
questions.explanation: « Tendre l'oreille » means to listen hard. The accent and expressions differed from what she expected, so she had to concentrate; nothing says she gave up on French.
